When the imam says Allah listens to him who praises Him, or ends the Fatiha, those behind respond with praise and Amin; whoever matches the angels is forgiven past sins.
Hurt by a fall from his horse or ill, the Prophet led prayer sitting and seated those behind: the imam is to be followed, never preceded, sitting when he sits.
In the Prophet's absence Abu Bakr and Abd al-Rahman b. Auf began leading the prayer before he arrived; to alert the imam men glorify Allah, while clapping is for women.
The Prophet forbade preceding the imam in bowing, prostration or standing, said he had seen Paradise and Hell, and warned Allah may turn a head raised first into an ass's.
The Prophet straightened the rows like an arrow, warning that crooked rows bring dissension among hearts, and wanted the sedate and prudent nearest him.
If people knew the first row's merit they would draw lots for it; men's best rows are first, women's last, and women were once told to lift heads after men.
When Mu'adh, after praying with the Prophet, led his people in a long night prayer with al-Baqara, the Prophet rebuked him for trying them and named shorter surahs to recite.
An imam must be brief for the weak, sick, aged and busy, but alone one may lengthen; the Prophet's prayer was brief yet perfect, shortened when a child cried.
Behind the Prophet no one bent down for prostration until he had placed his forehead on the ground; only then did they follow him.
When the iqama is said, come to prayer walking calmly, not running, pray what you catch with the imam and complete what you missed.
Whoever catches one rak'ah of the prayer, with the imam in one wording, has caught the prayer.
Prayer in congregation is twenty-five or twenty-seven degrees more excellent than prayer said alone.
The Prophet said he had thought of burning the houses of men absent from congregational and Friday prayers, and that the night and morning prayers weigh most on hypocrites.
A blind man hearing the call was told to answer it; Ibn Mas'ud said only known hypocrites or the sick stayed away; one leaving after the call disobeyed the Prophet.
Praying Isha in congregation is like praying half the night and the morning prayer like praying all night; whoever prays the morning prayer is under Allah's protection.
The Prophet led Anas and his household in prayer at home, Anas standing behind him with an orphan or alone at his right, and the women behind them.
Congregational prayer exceeds praying at home or market by over twenty degrees; each step to the mosque raises a degree, and angels pray for those waiting there in ablution.
The one best versed in the Quran leads the prayer, then the most knowing of the Sunnah, earliest emigrant or eldest; the Prophet told young visitors their oldest should lead.
Once the iqama is given only the obligatory prayer is prayed; the Prophet questioned men who prayed alone after the dawn prayer had begun.
On a journey the Prophet prayed in one garment tied at opposite ends and moved Jabir, standing behind him, to his right.
